items.description: Existing prepared sidecars have no explicit path to establish a concurrent-delivery relationship.
items.evidence: Existing records skip the creation step containing reciprocal-link instructions; activate and build require the link without creating it.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Allow an explicitly requested existing sidecar to be linked to a selected parent through a recoverable reciprocal update, without inferring a relationship.
items.rationale: A user must be able to explicitly establish reciprocal delivery links for an existing prepared sidecar; activation must not infer them.

items.description: Unsupported kinds still receive generic next actions in later lifecycle states.
items.evidence: The guard excludes only preparation states; later states fall through to the general status map.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Determine whether generic later-stage workflows apply to these kinds and constrain or diagnose unsupported routes consistently.
items.rationale: The consolidate-state-enums change will enumerate supported kinds and make unsupported kinds invalid.

items.description: The public lifecycle reference still describes the previous abbreviated workflow.
items.evidence: docs/LIFECYCLE.md retains direct bugfix/refactor execution and an outdated Mermaid transition.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Align the public reference with the current lifecycle and skill guidance, including the S-sized design path.
items.rationale: Public lifecycle documentation must reflect the implemented workflow, including abbreviated activation and the S-sized design skip.

items.description: Resolve still describes dispatching abbreviated execution via bugfix or refactor.
items.evidence: The named skill now hands off to build; the report does not establish that resolve fails to reconcile the resulting work.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Check resolve’s dispatch and reconciliation contract against the new handoff and clarify any real mismatch.
items.rationale: The authorised abbreviated workflow can delegate execution to build; no reconciliation failure was demonstrated.

items.description: The task claims verify and review guidance was reconciled although those files were not edited.
items.evidence: Neither file changed; lack of edits alone does not show that existing instructions are inconsistent.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Inspect the actual verification and review guidance and correct only demonstrable gaps or the task wording.
items.rationale: Existing verify and review support named non-selected abbreviated work; no conflicting instruction was identified.

items.description: Next-action reporting now interprets task completion in a new sidecar-specific parser.
items.evidence: The code parses Markdown tasks and fences, while normal building records report build without task inspection; progress is not proof of task completion.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Assess the parser against the agreed deterministic build behaviour and avoid competing task interpretations.
items.rationale: The reinstated refactor-change-record change owns a shared lazy-loaded record and next-action interpretation using lifecycle and artifact evidence.

items.description: Sidecar task plans are read sequentially when listing changes.
items.evidence: Each building abbreviated record is awaited during row construction; practical impact depends on workload.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Consider whether measured listing latency warrants concurrent reads, rather than adding concurrency speculatively.
items.rationale: No measured performance problem justifies introducing concurrency for these reads.

items.description: Activation refers to preparation mode without a clear entry point in abbreviated skills.
items.evidence: The owning skills describe a user request to prepare without execution, but activation has no explicit mechanism for passing that intent.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Make the preparation-only handoff explicit and ensure it returns to activation rather than executing or stopping ambiguously.
items.rationale: Explicitly define preparation-only invocation and return to activation before named build.

items.description: Prepare advertises activation while direct named bugfix/refactor invocation remains supported.
items.evidence: Different advertised and available entry points are not necessarily contradictory.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Clarify direct invocation only if the workflow is materially ambiguous; otherwise decline.
items.rationale: The remove-prepare-skill change will remove prepare and reconcile its callers and direct-entry guidance.
